Problem 590. Reading an archaeological sequence: case 5
Archaeological layers provide relative chronological information. Dates from objects add constraints but do not automatically make every date exact.

An undisturbed archaeological site has four layers from top to bottom: A, B, C, D. In an undisturbed sequence, lower layers were deposited earlier. D contains an object dated 1320, C contains one dated 1510, and B contains one dated 1680. Cross-domain check: a local committee has 13 members, requires at least 7 present for quorum, and 11 are present.

In an undisturbed sequence, a lower layer is older than a layer above it. A securely dated object provides a constraint on the layer that contains it, but one object does not date every other object exactly. For the cross-domain check, quorum exists when present members ≥ the stated threshold.
Which is older, Layer C or Layer B? Can the exact year of deposition of Layer A be deduced? Cross-domain check: is quorum met?

1. C lies below B, so C is older than B by the stratigraphic rule. 2. No exact dated object or deposition year is given for A. 3. Therefore only relative ordering, not an exact year for A, is justified. Cross-domain check: compare 11 with 7; 11≥7 is true.
Layer C is older than Layer B. The exact deposition year of Layer A cannot be deduced. Cross-domain answer: quorum is met.

Problem 591. Applying a rule with an exception: Eli
Rules often have conditions and exceptions. Logical reading prevents us from applying a general rule when an overriding exception is active.

Eli is 12 years old. A library rule says: a child may enter the archive room if age ≥ 13 AND an adult permit is present. Exception: during an evacuation drill, nobody may enter. Permit present: yes. Evacuation drill: no.
Check exceptions first if they override the general rule. Otherwise every condition joined by AND must be true.
May Eli enter the archive room under these facts? Show which conditions succeed or fail.
1. Age test: 12≥13 is False. 2. Permit test is True. 3. Because the general rule uses AND, both tests must pass. 4. Therefore entry is not allowed.
The order of reasoning matters when exceptions override ordinary rules.
Boolean rule with priority: exception predicate first, then conjunction of eligibility conditions.
